sections.h: His death, as Smyrna told it
sections.b: The Martyrdom of Polycarp, a letter of the church of Smyrna, tells how Polycarp withdrew to a farm, saw his pillow burning in a vision, was betrayed and arrested on a Friday, refused to say 'Lord Caesar' and sacrifice, and before the proconsul answered, 'For eighty-six years I have been his slave, and he has never wronged me' (9:3) and 'I am a Christian' (10:1). The fire would not burn him; he was stabbed, and his bones were gathered and honored, and the church planned to keep 'the birthday of his martyrdom' each year (18:3). It calls him 'an apostolic and prophetic teacher, overseer of the catholic church in Smyrna' (16:2).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 5:1-2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 8:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 9:3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 10:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 16:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 18:3

sections.h: 'The earliest known history of a Christian martyrdom'
sections.b: Lake calls the Martyrdom of Polycarp 'the earliest known history of a Christian martyrdom, the genuineness of which is unquestionable'; Bart Ehrman argues that it was written decades later. It uses the words martys, 'witness', and martyrion for dying for Christ throughout (1:1), and it sets out a teaching on martyrdom: martyrdom comes 'by the will of God' (2:1); one should not give oneself up, as Quintus did and failed (4:1); the martyr imitates the Lord's passion 'in line with the gospel' (1:1; 19:1); the martyrs are loved 'as disciples and imitators of the Lord' (17:3).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:1-2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 2:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 4:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 17:3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 19:1

sections.b: Smyrna gathered Polycarp's bones, 'worth more than costly gems', and planned a yearly gathering on 'the birthday of his martyrdom' (18:2-3), which the Catholic Encyclopedia's article on relics calls 'the classical instance' of their veneration.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 18:2-3

sections.h: The church of Smyrna in the Martyrdom
sections.b: Smyrna's church writes the Martyrdom of Polycarp to Philomelium (1:0). It shows a church of the 150s with its leader, its 'overseer' (16:2), under persecution from a crowd of 'Gentiles and Jews who lived in Smyrna' (12:2), facing the proconsul in the stadium, and keeping its martyr's bones and his yearly day (18:2-3). Revelation had promised this church 'the crown of life' (Revelation 2:10), and the Martyrdom speaks of Polycarp 'crowned with the crown of incorruption' (17:1).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:0; Martyrdom of Polycarp 12:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 16:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 17:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 18:2-3; Revelation 2:8-11

sections.b: 'For Christ we worship, because he is the Son of God. The martyrs we love as disciples and imitators of the Lord' (17:3). The Martyrdom of Polycarp draws the line between worship and honor, and records the gathering of Polycarp's bones and the plan for a yearly feast at his grave (18:2-3). The churches' views on what honor of the saints may include are on the cards at Acts 10, Revelation 5 and 2 Kings 13.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 13:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 17:1-3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 18:2-3

sections.b: Polycarp is urged to say 'Lord Caesar' and offer sacrifice (8:2), and to 'swear by the fortune of Caesar' (9:2; 10:1). He refuses: Christ is 'my King' (9:3), and the letter dates his death 'while Jesus Christ was reigning as King forever' (21:1). The crowd calls the Christians 'atheists' (3:2), and the Asiarch, a priest of the emperor's cult (LSJ), says he has closed the animal hunts (12:2).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 3:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 8:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 9:2-3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 10:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 12:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 21:1

sections.b: The proconsul of Asia tries Polycarp in the stadium, pleads with him to respect his age, swear and curse Christ, and threatens him with beasts and fire (9:2-11:2). The dating note names him Statius Quadratus (21:1), whose year in office is the key to dating the martyrdom.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 3:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 4:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 9:2-3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 10:1-2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 11:1-2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 21:1

sections.h: The Jews of Smyrna in the Martyrdom of Polycarp
sections.b: The letter names 'Jews' four times among Polycarp's enemies: in the crowd (12:2), eagerly gathering wood 'as is their habit' (13:1), urging that the body be withheld (17:2), and quarreling at the pyre (18:1). Revelation had already spoken of conflict at Smyrna (Revelation 2:9). Eusebius keeps all four lines. Whatever happened that day, the phrase 'as is their habit' blames a whole people.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 12:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 13:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 17:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 18:1; Revelation 2:9

sections.h: A death in line with the gospel
sections.b: The Martyrdom of Polycarp tells his death on the pattern of Jesus' passion: handed over (1:2), betrayed by his household (6:2), hunted by a Herod (6:2), arrested as if he were a bandit (7:1), 'May God's will be done' (7:1), entering the city on a donkey (8:1) on 'a great Sabbath'. Lake: 'The coincidences are remarkable, but none are in themselves at all improbable.'
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:1-2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 6:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 7:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 8:1

sections.b: Polycarp prayed night and day for 'the churches all over the world' (5:1), prayed aloud for two hours before his arrest (7:2-8:1), and at the stake gave thanks for his share in 'the cup of your Christ' (14:1-3).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 5:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 7:2-3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 8:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 14:1-3

sections.h: Glory with the Son and the Spirit
sections.b: Polycarp's last prayer ends: 'through him be glory to you, with him and the Holy Spirit, both now and for the ages to come' (14:3). Eusebius's copy reads 'with him, in the Holy Spirit', naming the Spirit as the one in whom glory is given (variant). The later notes give glory to the Father and the Holy Spirit (22:1; 22:3).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 14:3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 22:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 22:3

sections.b: Polycarp refuses to 'swear by the fortune of Caesar' (9:2; 10:1). Lake notes that Christians rejected this oath but would swear 'by the safety of Caesar', citing Tertullian, Apology 32. Quintus, who failed, was talked 'into swearing the oath and offering sacrifice' (4:1).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 4:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 9:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 10:1

sections.b: At the stake Polycarp thanks God for a share 'in the cup of your Christ' (14:2), which recalls the cup Jesus spoke of in Mark 10:38-39. The account does not name the Lord's Supper; whether its words of thanksgiving, cup, sacrifice and bread (15:2, a loaf that Eusebius's copy lacks) were meant to recall it is a question the text leaves open.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 14:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 15:2; Mark 10:38-39

sections.b: Polycarp was arrested on the Day of Preparation (Friday) and died on 'a great Sabbath' (8:1; 21:1), the phrase of John 19:31. Lake reports two views of which Sabbath it was: Purim, or the Sabbath after Passover by Smyrna's Jewish reckoning.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 7:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 8:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 21:1; John 19:31

sections.b: Like Stephen, the martyrs of Smyrna are strengthened by the Lord standing beside them (2:2; Acts 7:55-56), and Polycarp's face is 'full of grace' before his judge (12:1; Acts 6:15).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 2:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 12:1; Acts 6:15; Acts 7:55-56

sections.b: The Martyrdom of Polycarp calls the proconsul 'the tyrant' who tries to turn the martyrs to denial by torture (2:4), as 4 Maccabees calls Antiochus 'the tyrant'. The praise of endurance under torture (2:2-4) follows the pattern of 2 Maccabees 6-7 and 4 Maccabees.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 2:2-4; 2 Maccabees 7:1-42; 4 Maccabees 5:1

sections.b: The Martyrdom of Polycarp calls the church 'catholic', meaning worldwide: 'the whole catholic church throughout the world' (8:1; compare 1:0; 19:2). In 16:2 Polycarp is 'overseer of the catholic church in Smyrna', where some witnesses read 'holy'. Lake: if 'catholic' is right, these are 'the earliest clear examples of this use of the word (but cf. Ignatius, Smyrn. viii.)'.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:0; Martyrdom of Polycarp 8:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 16:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 19:2

sections.h: Honor to rulers, but not worship
sections.b: Before the proconsul, Polycarp says: 'we have been taught to give rulers and authorities appointed by God the honor that is due them, as long as it does us no harm' (10:2, after Romans 13:1 and 1 Peter 2:13). He reasons with the governor but refuses to swear by Caesar's fortune.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 10:2; Romans 13:1-7; 1 Peter 2:13-17

sections.h: The fire that lasts an hour
sections.b: 'You threaten a fire that burns for an hour and is soon put out. For you do not know the fire of the coming judgment and eternal punishment, which is kept for the ungodly' (11:2).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 2:3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 11:2

sections.b: Polycarp's prayer asks for 'the resurrection to eternal life, of soul and body, in the incorruption of the Holy Spirit' (14:2, after John 5:29).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 14:2; John 5:29

sections.b: Polycarp's prayer calls Jesus God's pais, 'servant' or 'child' (14:1; 14:3; compare 20:2), as the early prayers of Acts 4:27-30 do. Lake: 'Here it is clearly "Child"', and a gloss gives that sense.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 14:1; Martyrdom of Polycarp 14:3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 20:2; Acts 4:27-30

sections.b: According to the note at the end of the Martyrdom of Polycarp, Gaius copied the text 'from the papers of Irenaeus, a disciple of Polycarp' (22:2); the Moscow manuscript's ending adds that Irenaeus was in Rome when Polycarp died and heard a voice like a trumpet.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 22:2

sections.b: The Martyrdom of Polycarp calls him 'overseer of the catholic church in Smyrna' (16:2), one man as the church's head, where his own letter names only elders (Polycarp to the Philippians 1:0; 5:3). The site keeps 'overseer' in both.
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 16:2; Polycarp to the Philippians 5:3

sections.b: The Martyrdom is in no church's Bible. It was read and copied as an account for the yearly feast of Polycarp (18:3), and Eusebius quoted most of it in his Church History (4.15).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 18:3; Martyrdom of Polycarp 22:2-3

sections.b: The letter of the church of Smyrna about its overseer's death (Lake: 155, in a 'contemporary' account) is counted among the Apostolic Fathers; Lake calls it 'the earliest known history of a Christian martyrdom'. It is the only one of the group that is a story rather than a letter of teaching, and its notes trace its own copying from Irenaeus to Pionius (22:2-3).
sections.refs: Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:0; Martyrdom of Polycarp 20:2; Martyrdom of Polycarp 22:2-3
